---
title: "Use Apple Intelligence to clean up blurry photos on your iPhone"
subtitle: "Discover how to quickly sharpen fuzzy images using Apple's smart features, making your treasured memories clear again without needing extra apps."
category: "guide"
audience: "personal"
company: "Apple"
tool: "Apple Intelligence"
level: "beginner"

Blurry photos can be frustrating – a perfect moment captured, but just a little out of focus. Luckily, your iPhone, powered by Apple Intelligence, offers smart ways to clean up those fuzzy shots right in the Photos app. By the end of this guide, you'll be able to use your device's built-in smarts to bring clarity back to your favourite pictures.

## Before you start
-   **A compatible iPhone or iPad**: You'll need an iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 15 Pro Max, or an iPad with an M1 chip or later, running iOS 18 (or iPadOS 18/macOS Sequoia on compatible devices). Apple Intelligence is only available on these newer devices.
-   **Photos app**: This guide uses the standard Photos app that comes with your device.
-   **An internet connection**: Some advanced AI features might occasionally use cloud processing, so a stable internet connection is helpful.
-   **Roughly 5-10 minutes**: The process is quick, but finding the right photo and making adjustments might take a few moments.

## Step 1 — Find your fuzzy photo
To begin, you'll need to open the Photos app on your iPhone or iPad. Look for the colourful pinwheel icon on your home screen – it's typically pre-installed. Once you tap it, you'll see a grid of all the photos and videos stored on your device, usually organised by date. This is your personal library, ready for you to browse.

If it looks different: If you can't find the Photos icon, swipe down from the middle of your home screen to open Search, then type "Photos" and tap the app when it appears.

You'll know it worked when you see your collection of pictures and videos laid out on the screen.

## Step 2 — Select the blurry image
Now that you're in your Photos library, scroll through until you find a photo that looks a bit blurry or out of focus. Tap on this photo to select it. When you tap, the image will open up to fill your screen, letting you see the details (and the blurriness) more clearly. This full-screen view is crucial for making precise edits later.

If it looks different: If you accidentally tap the wrong photo, simply tap the back arrow in the top-left corner, or swipe right from the left edge of the screen, to return to your library and choose another one.

You'll know it worked when the blurry photo you want to fix is displayed large on your screen, ready for editing.
💬 Example: N/A (this step involves selecting an image)

## Step 3 — Activate the Edit menu
With your blurry photo displayed full screen, look for the "Edit" button. It's usually located in the top-right corner of the screen. Tapping "Edit" will switch your Photos app into editing mode, revealing a set of tools at the bottom of the screen. These tools allow you to make various adjustments to your image, from cropping to applying filters.

If it looks different: On some devices or iOS versions, the "Edit" button might look like a pencil icon or be located at the bottom of the screen. Look for any button that clearly indicates you'll be modifying the photo.

You'll know it worked when you see a row of icons (like a dial, a crop tool, and a magic wand) appear at the bottom of your screen, indicating you're in the photo editing interface.
💬 Example: N/A (this step involves an interface action)

## Step 4 — Tap the 'Enhance' or 'Adjust' option
Within the editing tools, Apple Intelligence quietly assists with smart enhancements. Look for a magic wand icon, usually towards the top or bottom of the screen, which often represents an 'Enhance' or 'Auto' feature. Tapping this icon will allow Apple Intelligence to automatically analyse your photo and suggest improvements to lighting, colour, and sharpness. If you prefer more control, look for the dial or slider icon at the bottom, which lets you access manual adjustment sliders like 'Sharpen' or 'Clarity'.

If it looks different: The exact icon for 'Enhance' might vary, or it could be a simple 'Auto' button. If a magic wand isn't visible, tap the dial/slider icon to view the full range of manual adjustments.

You'll know it worked when your photo shows a subtle visual improvement from the automatic enhancement, or the screen displays a list of specific adjustment options like 'Exposure' and 'Brilliance'.

## Step 5 — Sharpen the image with AI assistance
If you tapped the dial/slider icon, you'll see a list of individual adjustment options. Scroll through these until you find 'Sharpen' or 'Clarity'. Tap on this option, and a slider will appear, usually at the bottom of your screen. As you drag this slider left or right, Apple Intelligence works in the background, making complex adjustments to your photo's pixels. It targets blurry areas, enhancing edges and definition to make the image appear crisper and clearer without making it look unnatural.

If it looks different: Sometimes 'Sharpen' might be called 'Definition' or 'Detail'. Experiment with these similar options if 'Sharpen' isn't explicitly listed. Ensure you're looking for the slider dedicated to crispness, not just brightness or contrast.

You'll know it worked when the blurry parts of your photo become noticeably more defined and the overall image looks clearer on your screen as you move the slider.

## Step 6 — Compare and save your changes
Once you're happy with the clarity of your photo, you can quickly compare it to the original. To do this, simply touch and hold the image on your screen. It will temporarily revert to the original, unedited version. Release your finger to see your enhanced version again. When you're satisfied, tap the "Done" button, typically located in the top-right or bottom-right corner of the screen. This will save your clearer photo, replacing the original or saving a new version, depending on your Photos app settings.

If it looks different: The comparison feature might also be a toggle button that appears while in editing mode. If you can't find a "Done" button, look for a checkmark or a "Save" option.

You'll know it worked when the editing screen closes, and your now clearer photo is displayed in your Photos app, ready for you to admire or share.

## Common mistakes
-   **Forgetting to save**: After making all your changes, it's easy to just close the app.
    *   **Fix**: Always tap "Done" or the checkmark icon to ensure your edits are saved. If you don't, all your hard work will be lost.
-   **Over-sharpening the image**: Dragging the 'Sharpen' slider too far can make your photo look grainy or artificial, almost like it has a halo around objects.
    *   **Fix**: Use the slider subtly. It's often better to under-sharpen slightly than to over-sharpen. Compare frequently with the original (by touching and holding the image) to find a natural balance.
-   **Expecting miracles from a very blurry photo**: While Apple Intelligence is smart, it can't completely reconstruct a photo that was extremely out of focus to begin with.
    *   **Fix**: Understand the limits. This tool is best for photos with minor to moderate blur. If a photo is severely blurry, it might not be possible to make it perfectly clear, but you can often still improve it.

## What this means for you
-   **In everyday life:** You can quickly rescue those slightly fuzzy photos of family, pets, or beautiful landscapes that you thought were unusable. No more regretting that you didn't get a perfectly sharp shot; Apple Intelligence helps you clean it up and keep that memory alive.
-   **For your business or work:** If you take photos for social media, product listings, or internal reports, being able to quickly sharpen them on the go means your visuals look more professional and appealing without needing specialist software or advanced editing skills.
-   **If you're just getting started:** The easiest first move is to pick one photo that's just a little bit blurry, open it in Photos, tap "Edit," and try the magic wand 'Enhance' button. See how Apple Intelligence instantly improves it.

## Try it now
Grab your iPhone or iPad, open the Photos app, and find a picture that's just a little bit blurry. Tap "Edit," then try tapping the magic wand 'Enhance' button. See how quickly Apple Intelligence can make a noticeable improvement to your photo's clarity.
